key_insight: VersaCamVLA makes robotic VLA policies robust to changing camera setups by separating how camera views are represented from how actions are learned. This lets a single policy work across different numbers, poses, and arrangements of cameras without retraining from scratch.
problem_solved: Most VLA models assume a fixed set of cameras during training, so they can break when the number of cameras or their positions change at deployment. This paper addresses the brittleness of robot manipulation policies under variable camera configurations.
method: Learns a unified scene-token interface that converts an arbitrary set of posed RGB camera views into a shared representation.
Decouples camera-set representation from action prediction so the policy can generalize across camera counts and poses.
Uses the camera-configurable framework to support flexible deployment in manipulation tasks without requiring a fixed training-time camera layout.
impact: For practitioners, this reduces the engineering burden of matching training and deployment camera setups, making robotic policies easier to reuse across labs, robots, and environments. It also improves the practical robustness of VLA systems for real-world manipulation.

paper_title: VersaCamVLA: Camera-Configurable VLA Policies for Robotic Manipulation
